Board Changes
Debenhams Group (DEBS.L), an online platform for fashion, home and beauty, announces the following board changes, with immediate effect.
Iain McDonald has been reappointed to the Board as Non-Executive Chair of the Company. Iain served on the Board between June 2017 and February 2026, and the Board is pleased that he has agreed to provide his expertise and leadership qualities to the Group as it progresses in the next phase of its strategy.
Tim Morris will step down from the Board and his role as Chair with immediate effect. Tim joined the Board in May 2021 and the Board would like to thank him for his significant contribution and commitment to the Group during his tenure.
The Company is also pleased to announce the appointment of Michael Stewart and Stephen Rothwell as Independent Non-Executive Directors with immediate effect.
The changes are intended to align the composition of the Board with the Group's priorities for the next phase of its strategy. With the substantive elements of the operational turnaround now complete, the Board's focus moves to rebuilding equity value in the Group. Iain and Michael add significant further experience of the investment markets alongside that already provided by John Goold, Senior Independent Director, and their combined experience and networks are expected to support the Group in broadening and extending its shareholder base.
Stephen brings a wealth of technology experience, having founded and led an AIM-quoted technology business, and will provide valuable support to the Board as the Group continues to build a world-class, technology and AI-enabled platform supporting its capital-light business model. He is the founder of Eagle Eye Solutions Group PLC, the AIM-quoted digital marketing technology business, where he served as a director from February 2014 until April 2025. He is currently a director of Eagle Eye Technology Limited and Eagle Eye Holdings Limited, and brings extensive experience of technology, digital loyalty and scaling consumer-facing platforms.
Michael Stewart is a member of Chrysalis Investment Partners LLP, which he joined in March 2024, and was previously a member of 8C Capital LLP. He brings 13 years of experience in investment management and public markets as an investment professional. Michael has worked alongside founders, management teams and boards on growth strategy, M&A, capital raising and long-term value creation. During his early career, Michael worked as an associate at 8C Capital, an independent private equity firm investing in mid and upper mid-market European businesses. He then moved to be an equity analyst at Merian Global Investors, later Jupiter Asset Management. Most recently Michael was lead analyst for the investment adviser to Chrysalis Investments Limited, where he worked on investments in Starling Bank, Klarna, Featurespace, Smart Pension and Embark Group.
Dan Finley, Chief Executive Officer of Debenhams Group, commented:
"I would like to thank Tim for the significant and critical contribution that he has made to our turnaround. The business has been significantly strengthened during his tenure as Chair. We wish him all the very best in his future endeavours.
"We are pleased to strengthen the Board today with the appointments of Iain, Stephen and Michael. They bring significant experience in capital markets and advanced technology, which will benefit us as we continue to deliver our multi-year turnaround."
Tim Morris, outgoing Non-Executive Chair of Debenhams Group, commented:
"It has been a privilege to chair this business through such a pivotal period. My thanks go to Dan and the executive team, to my Board colleagues, and above all to every one of our employees, whose commitment and hard work have driven the turnaround. I leave the Group in good hands and wish Iain and the team every success in the next phase."
Iain McDonald, Non-Executive Chair of Debenhams Group, commented:
"It was a very difficult decision to step away from the Board of Debenhams earlier this year, and it is a great honour to be asked to return in the role of Chair. I am a material investor both personally and via the funds managed by my business, Belerion Capital Group, and this is a measure of the degree to which I believe in the potential of the business. The progress made over the past 6-12 months is significant and there is a real feeling of momentum in the business. I look forward to supporting the management team in their efforts to restore value and to engage constructively with all shareholders."

Trading update for the six months ended 31 August 2026
Growth Accelerated Through H1 with Record Marketplace Mix
Adjusted EBITDA up 14%, Reported EBITDA up 731%
H1 FY27 Trading Update
Our turnaround continues at pace. Momentum accelerated through the first half ended 31 August 2026 (“H1”). GMV grew 1.8% year on year, with growth of 0.5% in the first quarter (“Q1”) accelerating to 2.9% in the second quarter (“Q2”). Performance was most notable across the Debenhams brand, where GMV grew 14.1% to represent c.41% of Group GMV. Pretty Little Thing, boohoo and Karen Millen have all returned to growth.
The return to growth has been supported by a record marketplace mix, materially improved profitability and significantly improved cash flows.
Marketplace GMV reached 38.9% of Group GMV, up from 32.7% in the prior year. The Group’s brand partner ecosystem expanded to c.30k brands or partners. All brands have completed the transition to the marketplace model, and the Group’s ambition is for marketplace to represent well over 50% of GMV.
Gross margin expanded to 53.9% (H1 FY26: 51.9%), and the Group’s returns rate declined by c.4% in the period.
Adjusted EBITDA increased by 13.9% to £24m (H1 FY26: £21m), with Adjusted EBITDA margin of 5.9% (H1 FY26: 5.0%).
Exceptional costs reduced by 83.5% to £4m (H1 FY26: £24m). Reported EBITDA of £20m (H1 FY26: -£3m) is a £23m improvement on the prior year.
Capital expenditure fell by 33% to £5m year on year (H1 FY26: £8m). Net debt reduced to £102m (H1 FY26: £111m), £9m lower year on year, and cash flows improved significantly, with the cash outflow after capital expenditure and interest materially reduced year on year.

Post Period End
As announced on 10 September 2026, the Group completed the £90m disposal of the Sheffield automation and lease assignment, a significant step in the transition to an asset-light model. Fulfilment of the Group’s stocked product will transfer to a global 3PL provider. The total cost to fulfil going forward will be no more expensive than the cost incurred in Sheffield.
The Group has completed the disposal of the Nasty Gal brand and its associated intellectual property for $16m, as announced on 15 September 2026, further simplifying the Group’s brand portfolio and supporting the focus on Debenhams and the Group’s marketplace model.
Together, these transactions materially reduce the Group’s debt and net debt is expected to be negligible at year end.
Outlook
In respect of the full year, the Board expects to deliver GMV growth, and Adjusted EBITDA as previously guided and in line with consensus of no less than £59m representing double-digit growth year-on-year. Furthermore, the Board expects continued material improvement in Reported EBITDA, a return to positive profit before tax, free cash flow generation and negligible net debt.
The £100m fixed cost target remains on track, taking the cumulative reduction delivered by the management team to c.£200m.
Looking ahead,
material cost reductions are expected in FY28: depreciation reduced to £14m (FY27: £22m), interest reduced by at least c.£10m based on the current facility, with potential for a further reduction under a new financial facility, and lease costs reduced to £4m (FY27: £14m).
Dan Finley, Group Chief Executive Officer, commented:
“Our turnaround continues at pace. This is a strong first half and, importantly, one where growth accelerated as we went through it. Group GMV is up 1.8% for the half, but the shape matters more than the headline: growth of 0.5% in the first quarter became 2.9% in the second, marketplace mix has reached a record 38.9%, up from 32.7%. Gross margin is 53.9% against 51.9% last year and our returns rate is c.4% lower.
“With the cost programme ahead of plan, lease costs falling, and net debt down year on year, we are reiterating our guidance of double-digit Adjusted EBITDA growth and free cash flow in FY27. Since the half year end, the Sheffield distribution centre and Nasty Gal disposals mark a further significant step in reducing leverage, and we now expect net debt to be negligible at our February 2027 year end.”

Disposal of Nasty Gal for $16m
Debenhams Group is pleased to announce that it has completed the sale of the Nasty Gal brand, including the global intellectual property rights, to White Space Group New York, LLC, operating as WSG Brands ("WSG"), for a total cash consideration of US$16 million (the "Transaction").
Nasty Gal generated GMV of £12m in FY26 and Adjusted EBITDA of £0.4m. It is non-core and not material to the Group. The Transaction aligns with our strategy of transitioning to a marketplace-led business model that is capital-lite, and further strengthens the balance sheet following the £90m sale of the Group's Sheffield Distribution Centre, announced on 10 September 2026.
Dan Finley, Group Chief Executive Officer, said:
"Our turnaround continues at pace. The disposal of this non-core asset aligns with our strategy and further strengthens the balance sheet following the £90m sale of our Sheffield Distribution Centre."

latest.content:

Boohoo Group Plc

This announcement contains inside information for the purposes of the Market Abuse Regulation (EU) No. 596/2014 (as amended) as it forms part of the domestic law of the United Kingdom by virtue of the European Union (Withdrawal) Act 2018 (as amended).
For immediate release
10 September 2026
boohoo group plc
("Debenhams Group", the "Group" or the "Company")
Disposal of Sheffield Distribution Centre for £90m
Net debt to be reduced to a negligible level
The Debenhams Group turnaround continues at pace as it transitions to a marketplace-led business model that is capital-lite, stock-lite, cost-lite and cash generative. The Group's ambition is for the marketplace to represent well over 50% of GMV.
Consistent with this strategy, the Group announces that it has sold the automation in its Sheffield distribution centre and reassigned the lease to Primark Stores Limited for consideration of £90m (the "
Transaction
") in cash. £76.5m was received on completion and the remaining £13.5m will be received on vacant possession early next year.
Concurrently, the Group is entering into an agreement with a global 3PL provider that will enable it to continue to fulfil its stocked product as efficiently as it does today and will allow the Group to scale its Delivered by Debenhams fulfilment proposition beyond fashion.
The Transaction will result in the Company significantly deleveraging, and we now expect net debt to be negligible at our year-end (Feb '27).
Going forward, depreciation will reduce by c.£12m per annum (£3m of which related to a right-of-use asset), interest will reduce by at least £10m per annum and cash lease costs will reduce by c.£4m per annum.
As previously announced, the Company returned to GMV growth in Q1 and the Board is pleased to report that growth accelerated in Q2. We will provide a H1 trading update on 17 September 2026.
Dan Finley, Group Chief Executive Officer, commented:
"The Debenhams Group turnaround continues at pace, and this transaction helps accelerate our progress. As a result of the disposal, net debt is now expected to be negligible at our year-end (Feb'27). We are also pleased to report that GMV growth has accelerated in Q2."

company_30s.what_they_do: DEBS.L is a high‑street retailer that sells fashion, beauty and home products across a network of stores and an online platform.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The UK retail sector is still restructuring after the pandemic; a brand with a long‑standing customer base and strong store footprint can still generate revenue if it adapts. DEBS’s partnerships with niche beauty brands and its large physical presence give it a unique positioning against pure e‑commerce competitors.
company_30s.current_state: The company is in a rebuilding phase. It has announced a new licensing partnership with Revolution Beauty, a joint broker appointment, and a block listing update that hints at a possible relaunch. Cash flow is tight, but the management is actively seeking capital and restructuring its store portfolio.

rns_narrative: A series of corporate updates shows DEBS moving from a crisis mode toward a structured recovery. The AGM and annual report releases keep the market informed of financial health, while the block‑listing notice signals that the company is preparing to re‑enter the market or shift to a new listing structure.

Strategic moves such as the Revolution Beauty partnership and the sublease of a US distribution centre demonstrate an attempt to diversify revenue streams and reduce overhead. The appointment of a joint broker indicates a push for better liquidity and investor outreach.
Collectively these announcements paint a picture of a company that is still fighting but is taking concrete steps to stabilise operations and attract new capital.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Skeptical optimism – traders are waiting to see if the restructuring will translate into real cash flow.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Some bullish chatter focuses on the licensing deal and the upcoming trading update, suggesting that a positive earnings report could spark a rally.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bear voices point to the need for a £35m raise and the fact that the company has been subleasing assets, implying ongoing cash pressure and a potential risk of delisting.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone has shifted from outright pessimism (early 2026) to cautious hope after the recent partnership announcement, but overall engagement remains low.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker are flat – no public interest spikes, which is a good sign for a contrarian play because it means the market hasn’t yet priced in a reversal.

near_term_catalysts: The next trading statement (due in late September) could provide a clear earnings picture and confirm whether the new partnership is generating revenue.
If the company successfully raises capital in the planned £35m round, the influx of cash would reduce the risk of further store closures.
A breakout above the recent low on higher volume would signal that the market is beginning to trust the recovery narrative.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a volume spike of at least 150% of the 20‑day average, a price break of 2% above the 20‑day moving average, or a positive earnings surprise of >10% versus analysts’ expectations.
expect_next.timing_regime: If the current price is already 80‑90% below its all‑time high, we are in the early to mid‑stage of a deep crash. Confirmation of mean reversion will come when the stock trades above the 20‑day moving average with sustained volume and a positive earnings report.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The deep drop creates a high‑asymmetry opportunity. If the stock is roughly 85% down, a 10% rally would bring it back to 75% down – an 11% increase on the current price. Historically, such rebounds have produced 30‑50% upside once the crash is fully priced in.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The company still needs a sizeable capital injection and has a history of store closures. If the funding round fails or if earnings remain negative, the stock could stay trapped at its current depth or fall further.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: 20‑30% if the price recovers to mid‑level of the crash. Potential loss: capped at the current price because the company is already at the bottom of its swing.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the stock breaks above its 20‑day moving average with volume 150%+ of the 20‑day average. Allocate 10‑15% of the trading capital, set a stop 5% below entry, and trail the stop as the price moves higher.
